pattern.short_summary: A structured artifact is exposed as a traversable graph of positions that the user steps through with discrete commands, with the system's response delivered on a nonvisual channel.
pattern.definition: A structured artifact is exposed as a traversable graph of positions that the user steps through with discrete commands, with the system's response delivered on a nonvisual channel. Position within the structure is announced, so the user's location is part of the output rather than something read off a display. The artifact is not flattened into a single linear description.
pattern.structural_signature: The artifact is parsed into addressable nodes (items, points, layers, regions); the input surface is a small set of discrete move commands (next, previous, into, out of) plus queries; each move emits a nonvisual rendering of the node reached together with an orientation cue naming where in the structure that node sits. The load-bearing property is the *persistent cursor*: state is carried between commands so the same key means different things at different positions. Transplants to any structured content and any nonvisual channel — a directory tree read aloud, a menu stepped through by haptics.

dimension.category_description: How interaction crosses sensory, physical, spatial, embodied, or representational channels.
dimension.classification_boundary: The channel, embodiment, or rendering must be the load-bearing interface mechanism.
